correctness.rationale: Both competing-risk probabilities follow from independent exponential mortality and explicitly specified equal-mean passage densities; differentiate to obtain the sign of 4x−exp(x). The signed maximum H(a) has a strictly negative derivative, H(0)>0 and H(a)→−∞, giving exactly one mortality threshold. Branch monotonicity and the negative positive-mortality infinite-deadline limit give all cases, endpoint equalities and continuity limits. The seven-file package embeds a self-contained numerical checker that passed 5,824 supplementary assertions; numerical checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A natural survival-and-passage management endpoint depends jointly on mortality and deadline. Exact equality of mean passage time does not fix deadline success. The theorem supplies a non-obvious two-reversal phase and exact destruction threshold; this is a meaningful analytical benchmark for competing-risk models rather than a reformulation of a textbook mean comparison. Its relevance is theoretical, not a field recommendation.
